No. OpenAdmin is an open‑source model that runs locally (or on a server you control). The model itself is a fine‑tuned version of **gpt‑oss‑20b**, which is an open‑source implementation of GPT‑3‑like behavior. Because the code is open, there is no built‑in mechanism to forward your prompts or responses to OpenAI’s servers.

**What that means for you**

| Scenario | Where the data stays | Who can see it |
|----------|----------------------|----------------|
| You run OpenAdmin on your own machine or a private server | On that machine / server | You (and anyone with access to that machine) |
| You use a hosted OpenAdmin deployment (e.g., a SaaS offering) | On the provider’s infrastructure | The provider (and potentially anyone with access to that infrastructure) |

If you’re using a hosted version, the privacy policy of the hosting provider will dictate whether they log or forward data. If you’re running it yourself, your data never leaves your environment.

**Bottom line:** The OpenAdmin model itself does not send data to OpenAI. Any data transfer would come from the deployment platform you’re using. If you want absolute control, run it locally.
